author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Tens of thousands of demonstrators have taken to the streets across France to protest rising living costs, inequality and government spending policies.

A tourism office was set on fire in Lyon, while vehicles and a newspaper kiosk were torched in Paris. Police fired tear gas and stun grenades as clashes erupted in several cities, with more than 250 people arrested nationwide.

The demonstrations have brought together students, teachers, trade unions and members of the Yellow Vest movement. Protesters are demanding better school facilities, more teachers and greater investment in public services.

The unrest comes as the French government faces mounting pressure over its spending plans and growing criticism of police tactics. Protesters accuse officers of excessive force, while fears grow that demonstrations could continue ahead of next year's presidential election.

Al Jazeera's Rosie Burchard reports from Rennes, and Natacha Butler reports from Paris.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Twenty years ago, two Malaysian special forces policemen brutally murdered Mongolian woman Altantuya Shaariibuu, obliterating her body with C4 military explosives.

But the truth behind why they killed her has yet to be determined, leading to suspicions of a political conspiracy to silence her.

101 East travels to Mongolia, Malaysia, France and Australia to investigate allegations of interference in the criminal trial, Altantuya's suspected links to an allegedly corrupt submarine deal and claims by the policemen that they acted on the orders of convicted former Prime Minister Najib Razak, who vehemently denies any involvement in the murder.
